question.problem:
The level curves of the function $f(x,y)=\frac{x+y}{x}$ are given by $f(x,y)=c.$ Which of the following statements are true?

I. $c=-1$ gives the $x$-axis, excluding the origin

II. $c=0$ gives the $y$-axis, excluding the origin

III. $c=1$ gives the line $y=x,$ excluding the origin
question.worked_solution:
Setting $f(x,y)=c$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+y}{x} & =c \\ x+y & =cx \\ y & =(c-1)x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

- If $c=-1,$ the level curve is the line $y=-2x,$ excluding the origin. So, I is false.

- If $c=0,$ the level curve is the line $y=-x,$ excluding the origin. So, II is false.

- If $c=1,$ the level curve is $y=0,$ which is the $x$-axis (excluding the origin). So, III is false.

So, the correct answer is "None of the listed".
